entries.text_en:
British Museum Regius 11 B II Liber monasterii Wygornie2, written c. 1160, beautifully but thoughtlessly, often still preserving ę for ae. Fol. 103—166 Quadripartitus of the middle edition, begins with Arg 32, below, p. 53511; I. II Cn, below, p. 279; f. 118b Af-Ine, below, p. 17; f. 136b I. II As, below, pp. 147. 151; f. 140b (after II As 23, 2) Ordal, below, p. 386; f. 142 Episc, below, p. 477; f. 143 Norðleod, below, p. 459; f. 143b Geþyncðo, below, p. 457; f. 144 Mirce; Að; Had, below, p. 463 ff.; f. 145 Blas; Forf, below, p. 389; f. 145b Hu, below, p. 192; f. 146 IV As, below, p. 171; f. 147b VI As, below, p. 173; f. 151b EGu from 9 onwards, below, p. 13327; f. 152 II Em, below, p. 187; f. 153 Swer, below, p. 397; f. 153b Wif, below, p. 443; f. 154b Wer, below, p. 393; f. 155 III Atr, below, p. 228; f. 156b Pax; Wal, below, pp. 391. 393; f. 156b IV Atr, below, p. 232; f. 158b II Atr, below, p. 221; f. 160b Duns, below, p. 375; f. 162 Iudex, below, p. 474; f. 163 Rect, below, p. 444; f. 166 Wl lad, below, p. 483.

There follows in the same hand Odo Cameracensis [† 1113] De canone missae3.

R was copied in Lh.

notes.text_en: f. 128 a letter from Worcester in chalk, 13th century. Cf. my Quadripartitus p. 61 f.

transcription.doubts: Superscript 11 (535<sup>11</sup>) and 27 (133<sup>27</sup>) are line references, not footnote marks (the page has no notes 11 or 27). The ę in 'ę für ae' is an e-caudata; whether it and 'ae' are italic is not certain (they look italic). 'u S. 444' printed without the period after u.
proof_notes: n. 2 text_en: 'in drypoint [lit. 'in chalk']' → 'in chalk' (interpretation not in the German)

wormald.other_contents: Added at Worcester to canon-law materials; also a list of the 'Seven Wonders of the World' and poetry of Hildebert of Tours (different hand). Calligraphic; frequent scribal lapses; omits and displaces items; dispenses with preliminary rubric lists (pp. 238–9 and n. 311).
wormald.overview: A handsome Worcester copy of Quadripartitus from the third quarter of the twelfth century, bound there with canon law and with literary pieces. It represents the second of the five stages Wormald identifies (after the version used by the London collection), omits or moves several texts, and for all its calligraphy is careless in detail.
wormald.key_quote: R (3) was added in its Worcester home to a collection of canon law materials (p. 238)
wormald.doubts: Guide date c. 1160 (Liebermann) is compatible with Wormald's s. xii^3/4.
